result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and wide, well-maintained sidewalks. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and warning signs are present, there is a lack of dedicated pedestrian signal heads and physical refuge for the crossing.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signal
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.
hazards.location_in_image: At the signal poles on both sides of the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Turning Vehicle Conflict
hazards.description: Signage indicates a risk of turning vehicles failing to yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left signal pole with 'Turning Vehicles Yield to Pedestrians' sign.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety for crossing.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The street features a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides, but lacks active traffic control or pedestrian signals. Parked vehicles along the curb create potential sightline issues for pedestrians attempting to cross the two-lane roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked cars on both sides of the street near the crosswalk block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Both curbs adjacent to the foreground crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk has no accompanying stop signs, traffic lights, or pedestrian warning signs to alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crosswalk to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs or Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) to alert drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with high-visibility zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like signals and curb ramps are present, the lack of curb extensions and the presence of parked cars near the crossing create potential visibility issues.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the crosswalk limit the visibility between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs approaching the intersection on both sides of the street.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the full width of the street without a refuge island or curb extensions to shorten the exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: The main roadway crossing in the foreground.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the crosswalk, improving visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals, providing essential infrastructure for walkers. However, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions or refuge islands increase pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Excessive crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to spend a significant amount of time in the path of vehicles without a mid-point refuge.

hazards.name: Lack of physical protection
hazards.description: There are no physical barriers or curb extensions to protect pedestrians at the corners or reduce the turning radius of vehicles.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a raised island in the center of the road to provide a safe waiting area for pedestrians mid-crossing.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to allow pedestrians to enter the crosswalk before vehicle traffic receives a green light.
